Achieving goals. Whether they be financial, or personal, or emotional.

There are multiples areas of success, you can succeed in some things and fail in others. At the end of the day you have to decide what you want to succeed in and what successes make you happy. There is nothing wrong with "failing" if that is your choice.

Not worrying about money. Lack of stress. Working at something that I either enjoy and challenges me-- something that doesn't feel like a waste of time... you know that awful 'living for the weekend' kind of mentality.
Having an idea and making it happen. Feels so good.

Honestly, happiness and satisfaction.

This includes having a job that enables you to have a lifestyle that you are happy and satisfied with, but not having to work to crazy stress levels to achieve it. Or having a job that you don't mind working a lot in. And I don't mean just making a lot of money. Many people can be perfectly happy making a medium amount of money as long as it enables a life that you are satisfied with, whether that is having a family or remaining single and living on your own.

Whatever brings you the most happiness is success, and it is different for everyone, so it is inherently difficult to put a definition on.

Being able to wake up excited for the day 90% of the time, everyone has those crap days or hangovers where you just want to stay in bed. I'm a college student working at a grocery store for a manager that treats me like crap, and I dread having to go but I need to pay for school. But I have a second job where I do IT for small small businesses and schools and on those days I wake up and am excited to just get the day going because I do what I love and get to help people that appreciate me. Even if it isn't work, everyone should have a reason that gets the excited for the day, once you get to that point I consider you successful.

It isn't about how much money you make or how big of an impact you as an individual has on the world. It's about putting the most important people in your life first always, no matter what. Enjoy what you have while you have it. Try to suppress your gags. It's cliche but the older I get the more true it seems to me. Someday we're all going to be dead and our personal goals will mean nothing. Only the impact we had on those around us will leave any kind of an imprint.
Being able to give myself a blowie. Will save a lot of time and money!

Whether or not common people speak and know your name 500+ years after you die. If you have an impact that large in the minds of the masses you were clearly successful at whatever you were doing.

Man that's a tough one. It used to be money but now that I'm comfortable and don't have to worry about my checking account balance it's become more about quality of life. I used to be all about my job but now I treasure every moment with my wife, friends, and my dog. Once you hit a certain age you start to see people divorce, get ill, get injured, die, and so on. It makes you realize that life is a short ride.

I want a stress free life filled with precious memories.
Living on your own with a job that can pay for your hobbies and no debt.
Being able to do nothing all of the time.
Enough money to provide for my family and give my to-be kids more opportunity than I had. Freedom and mobility in work and joy in my everyday life.
not living in a cardboard box, honestly.

Personally, I feel successful when I get over an obstacle. Whether it is beating a hard boss in a videogame or improve my health/financial condition/etc. up to a new benchmark, constantly completing personal goals give me a feeling of success.
Doing what you love and loving what you do. It's cliché but true.
Getting paid for doing that which you would do for free anyway, just because you enjoy doing it.

Hola a todos quería saber que opinan sobre el inesperado regalo de Evo Morales presidente de Bolivia al Sumo Pontífice, sumo noticia del sitio INFOBAE

Tensión se vivió en la primera jornada de Francisco en Bolivia. Es que el presidente boliviano decidió regalarle al Santo Padre una particular "cruz comunista".

El Papa acababa de llegar a La Paz. Después del gran recibimiento en el aeropuerto y de unos 10 minutos de descanso –porque la ciudad boliviana está a 3.600 metros de altura y eso desgasta la salud de cualquier visitante–, se dirigió al Palacio del Quemado para una reunión protocolar con el mandatario.

La transmisión en directo del sitio de YouTube del Vaticano mostró, aunque con sonido ambiente, la pequeña ceremonia en que el boliviano le entregaba obsequios. Aun cuando no se podía escuchar bien lo que decían, sí se entiende con claridad la frase del Papa cuando recibe el particular crucifijo: "No está bien eso".

Luego de la incomodidad papal, la jornada continuó y en una cálido mensaje a los feligreses en la catedral Nuestra señora de La Paz, Francisco pidió "un indispensable diálogo" entre Bolivia y Chile en el diferendo internacional sobre la salida al océano Pacífico.
